id: title:jurajmajerik:skip sizing request when ratio retention baseline lacks denominator stats

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a frontend-side guard to prevent unnecessary API requests when baseline statistics are missing, potentially reducing frontend-to-backend traffic and avoiding failed request handling.
review.reason: The change adds a new exported function `hasRequiredBaselineStats` and its unit tests, along with its usage in the running time calculation flow. This checks whether baseline stats are sufficient before proceeding, preventing the frontend from making requests that would be rejected by the backend due to missing denominator stats. This is a localized frontend implementation and test
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on the frequency of such low-data experiments and the backend's rejection behavior, which are not demonstrated in this frontend-only chunk. No backend compatibility or shared dependency is shown.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a frontend-only implementation and test addition. It does not demonstrate backend compatibility, shared dependency, or actual customer benefit. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new exported function hasRequiredBaselineStats and its unit tests, and its usage in the running time calculation flow.
observations.posthog_connection: Checks whether the baseline stats are sufficient to size this metric type. Ratio and retention sizing needs the baseline's denominator stats; low-data experiments return denominator_sum as null or 0, which the backend rejects — callers should skip the request rather than fire a doomed one.
